collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 4-9)

collection.description: A small child trips and knocks over a villager's shrine and waits for shouting: help the child up, or let them make it right.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) keeps a little shrine by (subject.his/her) door: carved figures, shells, a bowl of water. (friend), a small child running past, trips and sends the whole thing flying. Shells everywhere. A figure cracked. (friend) freezes, white-faced, waiting for shouting.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) picks (friend) up and checks (friend.his/her) knees. "Are you hurt?" (friend) shakes (friend.his/her) head, nearly crying. "I broke it." "It was an accident," says (subject). "Will you help me put it back?" They pick up the shells together. The cracked figure gets a little binding of string. (subject) says it looks even better now. (friend) isn't sure about that, but feels a lot better.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "It's alright," says (subject). "But would you like to help fix it?" (friend) nods hard. (friend.He/she) spends all afternoon carefully arranging the shells, adding a few of (friend.his/her) own, and drawing a little picture in the sand in front. When (friend.he/she) finishes, (friend.he/she) looks up anxiously. (subject) studies it seriously. "It's beautiful," (subject.he/she) says. "Thank you." (friend) glows.
